screening_decisions.reason: RCT of intracervical nitroprusside gel versus placebo for reducing IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women; meets all selection criteria.
Randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial of prophylactic ibuprofen 800 mg for pain with IUD insertion; pain is the primary outcome.

The study evaluates bladder filling to assist insertion, not an intervention specifically intended to prevent IUC insertion‑related pain. Its primary focus is ease of insertion rather than pain reduction.
RCT comparing intracervical lidocaine injection to oral ibuprofen for pain during LNG‑IUS insertion; both arms are active interventions for pain prevention.
Double‑blind, placebo‑controlled RCT of ibuprofen 800 mg prophylaxis for pain at LNG‑IUS insertion; self‑reported pain measured.
Double‑blind, multicenter RCT of vaginal misoprostol (cervical ripening agent) versus placebo before IUD insertion; pain is a primary outcome.
RCT of buccal misoprostol 400 µg versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; patient‑reported pain assessed with VAS.
Double‑blind, placebo‑controlled RCT of sublingual misoprostol for repeat LNG‑IUS insertion; evaluates ease and pain, misoprostol is a relevant cervical ripening intervention.
Large double‑blind RCT of prophylactic ibuprofen 400 mg versus placebo for copper IUD insertion pain in first‑time users; pain measured with VAS.
Single‑blind RCT of sublingual misoprostol plus diclofenac versus diclofenac alone before IUD insertion in women without vaginal delivery; pain and ease outcomes.
Double‑blind RCT of ibuprofen (prostaglandin synthesis inhibitor) versus placebo for IUD insertion; pain assessed at multiple time points.
RCT comparing two oral analgesics (tramadol and naproxen) and placebo for pain relief during IUD insertion; meets criteria as an active‑comparator trial.
Double‑blind RCT of self‑administered misoprostol versus placebo for cervical ripening before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; pain is a measured outcome.
RCT of intracervical 2 % lidocaine gel versus placebo for pain during IUD insertion; evaluates a local anesthetic intervention.
Pilot RCT of vaginal nitroglycerin gel versus placebo for reducing IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women; evaluates a pharmacological pain intervention.
RCT comparing 1 % lidocaine paracervical block to no anesthetic for pain during IUD insertion; evaluates a local anesthetic technique.
Randomized double‑blind trial of lidocaine gel versus lubricant gel versus no intervention for copper IUD insertion pain; local anesthetic for pain prevention.
Randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled pilot RCT of intrauterine lidocaine infusion versus saline for reducing IUD insertion pain.
RCT of sublingual misoprostol versus diclofenac alone for cervical priming before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; pain and ease evaluated.
Double‑blind RCT of vaginal misoprostol versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulligravidas; primary outcomes include pain and ease of insertion.
RCT of inhaled lavender aromatherapy versus placebo for anxiety and pain during IUD insertion; evaluates a complementary intervention for pain prevention.
RCT of self‑administered misoprostol versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; pain is a measured outcome, misoprostol is a cervical ripening agent.
Randomized placebo‑controlled trial of a novel topical lidocaine formulation for pain during IUD insertion; meets all inclusion criteria.

The study is described as a prospective, single‑blinded, controlled study but does not state that participants were randomly allocated. This does not meet the review’s inclusion criterion of randomized controlled trials.
Registered RCT of misoprostol versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; primary outcome is insertion pain.

RCT evaluating self-administered lidocaine gel vs. placebo for reducing pain during IUD insertion. Assesses pain at tenaculum placement and IUD insertion, matching primary outcomes. Meets all inclusion criteria.
Not an RCT; describes the author's clinical experience with intracervical block without a controlled comparison group. Does not meet study design criterion.
Prospective cohort study, not an RCT. Compares pain between groups but does not evaluate an intervention. Excluded due to study design.
Qualitative study exploring perceptions, not an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUD insertion pain. Excluded due to study design and irrelevant outcomes.
Narrative review/consensus recommendations, not an original RCT. Excluded due to study design.
Methodological article on GRADE, not related to IUD insertion pain interventions. Excluded due to irrelevant topic and study design.
Clinical guideline/committee opinion, not an RCT. Does not evaluate an intervention for IUD insertion pain. Excluded.
Narrative review of pain management strategies, not an original RCT. Excluded due to study design.
Review article on misoprostol uses in gynecology, not an original RCT specifically on IUD insertion pain. Excluded due to study design and lack of original data.
Not described as an RCT; appears to be a single-arm observational study evaluating a technique without a randomized comparison group. Excluded due to study design.
GRADE methodology guideline, not a study on IUD insertion pain. Excluded due to irrelevant topic.
Nonrandomized study assessing predictors of insertion difficulty, not an intervention trial. Excluded due to study design.
Review/discussion article, not an original RCT. Excluded due to study design.
Systematic review, not an original RCT. Although it includes RCTs, it is not itself an eligible primary study. Excluded.
Observational study using questionnaires; women self-selected analgesia. Not an RCT. Excluded due to study design.
Technical report/policy statement on adolescent contraception, not an RCT on IUD insertion pain. Excluded due to irrelevant topic and study design.
Meta-analysis of RCTs, not an original RCT. While it synthesizes relevant evidence, it is not a primary study. Excluded.
RCT but population is women undergoing surgical abortion, not IUD insertion. Does not evaluate pain during IUD insertion. Excluded due to wrong population/outcome.
Survey of clinician practices, not an RCT. Excluded due to study design.
Methodology paper describing planned meta-analysis, not original research. Excluded due to study design and lack of outcome data.
Commentary/review arguing against misoprostol use, not an original RCT. Excluded due to study design.

RCT but evaluates meptazinol for treatment of post-insertion pain (given after insertion), not for prevention of insertion-related pain. Does not meet criterion of evaluating an intervention for preventing IUC insertion pain.
Clinical trial with random assignment to lavender aromatherapy, placebo, and control, assessing pain during IUD insertion. Meets criteria for RCT evaluating an intervention for IUD insertion pain.
Descriptive report of a technique, not an RCT. Excluded due to study design.
Cochrane systematic review, not an original RCT. Excluded due to study design.
